policy.purpose: Record independent source-identity and claim-scope review for heldout-v3 candidates before any benchmark promotion.
requirements: source DOI or publisher identity resolves to the cited work
candidate expected_points stay within the cited experiment's reported scope
universal cultivation prescriptions are not inferred from experiment-specific findings
review does not itself promote the candidate benchmark

reviews.notes: Publisher article reports higher inflorescence yield at higher tested PPFD, no light-intensity effect on inflorescence cannabinoid concentration, and no commercially relevant UV benefit under the tested treatments.

Publisher article reports visual Mg-deficiency symptoms and impaired function at the lowest Mg supply in controlled vegetative-stage plants; candidate correctly treats appearance as compatible evidence rather than a standalone diagnosis.
Publisher abstract reports moderate drought did not significantly change yield or THC/CBD concentrations, while severe drought reduced yield and cannabinoid concentrations with cultivar variation.
Publisher article reports 25 mg/L P was sufficient for maximum yield and cannabinoid concentration under the experiment and higher P increased leachate P without improving yield or quality.
Publisher article evaluates six spectra in one accession; candidate appropriately refuses a universal best spectrum and distinguishes concentration from total compound yield.

Publisher article reports amino-acid supplementation altered ionome and secondary metabolites, including reduced cannabinoid-acid content and increased selected monoterpenes, and calls for further dosage/media/chemotype work.

Publisher article concludes the tested short-wavelength UV treatments did not increase yield or cannabinoid concentration and had no commercially relevant secondary-metabolite benefit in the two studied cultivars.

Publisher article reports impaired function/yield at 15 mg/L K, generally favorable function/yield across higher tested levels, genotype-specific responses, and suggests 60 mg/L only within the studied reproductive-stage conditions.
APS Plant Disease report documents HLVd detection in symptomatic Cannabis and experimental infectious-RNA evidence; the benchmark keeps symptoms non-specific and requires molecular confirmation.
APS Plant Disease report documents multiple Botrytis species associated with hemp flower disease in Oregon; the benchmark therefore avoids species-level diagnosis from appearance alone.

APS Plant Disease report verifies the Oregon Cannabis powdery-mildew source identity and laboratory-supported identification; the benchmark requires provenance-preserving citation rather than image-only species claims.

Peer-reviewed Viruses article reports RT-PCR detection, infectivity assays and seed transmission in tested hemp material; the benchmark preserves the experiment-specific scope of the reported transmission rates.

Frontiers article reports cultivar-specific transpiration-normalized nutrient uptake and explicitly discusses limitations of leaf-only tissue concentration for whole-plant nutrient status; benchmark keeps values conditional on the study context.
